lessons.summary: The source introduces preservation and high-temperature treatment; its chilling and freezing lectures are referenced attachments that were not supplied.

sections.heading: METHODS OF FISH PRESERVATION
sections.content: Preservation is a very important aspect of the fisheries. Normally the fish farms or other fish capturing sites are located far off from the market place and there is chance of fish decomposition and the uncertainties of their sale in market. When the fishe s are caught in numbers, greater than the amount of consumption, their preservation becomes a necessity for their future use. Preservation and processing, therefore become a very important part of commercial fisheries. It is done in such a manner that the fishes remain fresh for a long time, with a minimum loss of flavor, taste, odor, nutritive value and the digestibility of their flesh. Freshness is usually judged in the trade entirely by appearance, odor and texture of the raw fish.

sections.heading: TEMPERATURE CONTROL
sections.content:
TEMPERATURE CONTROL

1. Chilling Please refer to the attached file for the lecture part.

2. Freezing Please refer to the attached file for the lecture part.

3. Use of High Temperature A method of preserving fish by the use of high temperature in a hermitically sealed container sufficient to kill pathogens and render spoilage microorganisms and enzymes inactive.

sections.heading: Types of heat treatments
sections.content:
Types of heat treatments

a) Pasteurization – A mild treatment given to foods that do not support the growth of highly resistant microorganism. Heat treatment sufficient to kill pathogens and most vegetative cells; spores may survive

b) Sterilization – A severe heat treatment given to foods capable of supporting the growth of heat resistant microorganisms. A process designed to destroy virtually all microorganisms regardless of their heat resistance. Any survivors will be spores incapable of reproducing under normal conditions. Absolute sterilization – destruction of all microorganisms vs. Commercial sterilization – Temperature of 110oC - 130 oC are used to destroy or render inactive all microorganisms that could cause toxicity or spoilage

key_concepts.definition: A mild treatment sufficient to kill pathogens and most vegetative cells; spores may survive, according to the source.
A severe heat treatment described in the source as designed to destroy virtually all microorganisms regardless of heat resistance.

lessons.title: USE OF PACKAGING TECHNOLOGIES
lessons.summary: The source describes modified-atmosphere and vacuum packaging and gives gas-mixture and gas-to-product ratios.

sections.heading: USE OF PACKAGING TECHNOLOGIES
sections.content: USE OF PACKAGING TECHNOLOGIES Packaging technologies involving either the replacement of air by certain gases (such as, CO 2, O2, N2 or combination of all) termed as modified atmosphere packaging (MAP) or removal of air and thus reducing the headspace to possible minimum (Vacuum packing VP) has been used in the preservation of muscle and plant foods. The use of packaging material with low gas and water permeability is very crucial in such technologies in order to prevent the exchange of gases between the interior and exterior of the packaged product and thus maintain the right atmospheric conditions around the product. The preservative effect of such technology is based on the atmospheric condition they create around the product. This condition establishes a significant hurdle for most strictly aerobic and facultative spoilage microorganisms. Moreover, lipid oxidation ca n also be prevented to some extent. Anon recommended that the retail pack for lean fish and shell fish to be composed of a mixture of CO 2:N2:O2 in a ratio of (40:30:30) and CO2:N2 (60:40) for fatty and smoked fish. The gas:product ratio of MAP packed fish is also recommended to be in the range of 2:1–5:1, where CO2 concentration can be maintained between 20–100%

key_concepts.definition: Replacement of air by certain gases or combinations of gases.
Removal of air to reduce headspace to the possible minimum.

lessons.title: REMOVAL OF MOISTURE
lessons.summary: The source describes natural and artificial drying and its stated moisture condition for storage.

sections.heading: REMOVAL OF MOISTURE
sections.content: REMOVAL OF MOISTURE Drying involves dehydration i.e. the removal of moisture contents of fish, so that the bacterial decomposition or enzymic autolysis does not occur. When moisture contents reduce up to 10%, the fishes are not spoiled provided they are stored in dry conditions. Fish drying is achieved either naturally or by artificial means. In natural drying the fishes after being caught are washed and dried in the sunshine. In artificial drying the killed fishes are cleaned, gutted and have their heads removed. They are then cut lengthwise to remove large parts of their spinal column, followed by washing and drying them mechanically.

lessons.title: OTHER PROCESSING METHODOLOGIES
lessons.summary: The source describes ozonation, three irradiation dose categories, and pickling.

sections.heading: Ozonation
sections.content: Ozonation: Ozone has been studied for its potential in disinfecting and improving the sensory quality of seafoods. Gonçalves stated that antimicrobial effect of ozone depends on its concentration, contact time, temperature and the production system used. According to Gonçalves, low concentrations of ozone in solutions can decrease the half–life of ozone and thus weakening its bactericidal effect.

sections.heading: Irradiation
sections.content: Irradiation: Irradiation in foods is described in three different ways that do not involve heat treatments. Radurization (cold pasteurization) involves the use of low doses (<1kGy) which inactivates non –spore forming bacteria. Radicidation reduce the number of viable and non –spore forming pathogenic bacteria and parasites using intermediate doses (2 –8kGy). Radappertization (cold sterilization) is used to eliminate highly pathogenic bacteria such as, Clostridium botulinum at high doses (>10kGy). (Note: kGy = kilogray, unit of measurement of radiation absorbed dose. Source: https://www.aqua-calc.com/)

sections.heading: Pickling
sections.content: Pickling: Pickling is one of the safest means of preservation of fish. Pickles prepared from fish are gaining acceptance in recent days, since they add to the palatability to starch based bland tasting Asian dishes; besides being nutritious. Fish pickles are good appetizers too. At present there is an expanding export and domestic market for fish pickles. It is prepared by cutting the edible portion of the fish into small pieces, followed by deep frying in vegetable oil and are subsequently mixed with vineg ar and salt for preservation, along with fried condiments and species for flavor development. The material is then generally kept for a minimum of 24 hrs for maturing before packing.

key_concepts.definition: Kilogray, a unit of measurement of radiation absorbed dose, as defined in the source note.
